rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for direct and indirect questions about time.
Use this formal or written alternative to 幾時 in questions about time.

example.english: When would it be convenient for you to meet?
example.jyutping: nei5 ho4 si4 fong1 bin6 zip3 gin3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for ordinary “when” meaning during or whenever the event occurs.

example.english: When you get home, remember to call me.
example.traditional: 你返到屋企嘅時候，記得打畀我。
example.jyutping: nei5 faan1 dou3 uk1 kei2 ge3 si4 hau6 gei3 dak1 daa2 bei2 ngo5

rows.note: Use this for the “as soon as” or repeated “whenever” reading, especially when one event immediately follows another.

example.english: When I get home, I take a shower right away.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 faan1 dou3 uk1 kei2 zau6 cung1 loeng4

rows.note: Use this when English “when” has the conditional meaning “if.”

example.english: When it rains tomorrow, we’ll cancel the event.
example.traditional: 如果聽日落雨，就取消個活動。
example.jyutping: jyu4 gwo2 ting1 jat6 lok6 jyu5 zau6 ceoi2 siu1 go3 wut6 dung6

rows.note: Use this explicit time-clause construction when English has a relative “when” clause; Cantonese often omits it instead.

example.english: When you get home, remember to call me.
example.traditional: 你返到屋企嗰陣時，記得打畀我。
example.jyutping: nei5 faan1 dou3 uk1 kei2 go2 zan6 si4 gei3 dak1 daa2 bei2 ngo5

rows.jyutping: dou3 A go2 zan6 si4 B
rows.note: Use this for a later point referred to as “at which time” or “when that time comes.”

example.english: When you graduate, we should have already moved house.
example.traditional: 到你畢業嗰陣時，我哋應該已經搬咗屋。
example.jyutping: dou3 nei5 bat1 jip6 go2 zan6 si4 ngo5 dei6 jing1 goi1 ji5 ging1 bun1 zo2 uk1
